subject: hyper-handoff

commit.note: Runs 1 and 2 and both cold reads were made on the skill text at main daf0b2d5. Run 3 was made on the text at dev f866f9d8, which includes commit a7d4efb3 and the review fixes. Run 4 was made on the text at 5ac4a9db, the wording fix for the two rows that failed run 3. Run 5 was made on the text at d65f97df, which adds the stale-fingerprint clause after 5-call rounds on 53b37388 and b77dc8a5 failed rows. Run 6 was made on the text at c479eead, which moves the trigger and the plain-continue exclusion into the first sentence; its cases were pinned in de94f823 and 400c9a4d before that text was written. The labels inside the raw files 07 and 08 name 011ce5ec, the hash of that wording commit before the branch was rebased onto dev 7bf50b8f; on dev it is c479eead (the case commits 47c6c617 and e8aea1a1 are de94f823 and 400c9a4d).

method.harness: scripts/measure-skill-trigger.mjs in this repository (bun), run with omp -p --no-session. Runs 1-2 used /tmp/handoff-eval-run/run.py and runs 3-4 run.py or run4.py; the routing prompt and catalog selection are the same. Run 5 uses 5 calls per case, retries a timed-out call twice, and passes a trigger row at 4/5 hits or more and a no_trigger row at 1/5 or fewer.
method.selection: The prompt lists every skill's name and description taken from the SKILL.md frontmatter, gives the case prompt, and asks for exactly one skill name or none.
method.passRule: A trigger case passes when at least 2 of 3 runs answer hyper-handoff; a no_trigger case passes when fewer than 2 do.
method.caseSource: skills/hyper-handoff/assets/evals/hyper-handoff-cases.jsonl, 19 cases for runs 1 and 2, 36 cases for runs 3 and 4
method.coldRead: A fresh omp -p --no-session session was given the memo only and asked what is being done and what the next step is, then answered the six questions.
method.runtime: run 3: omp/18.18.5; run 4: omp/18.18.6; the runtime version of runs 1 and 2 was not recorded
method.observedValues: hyper-handoff, none, other-skill for any other skill name in the catalog, and unparsed for a reply that was neither a catalog name nor none; unparsed appears in runs 3 and 4 and counts as not hyper-handoff; run 6 also records transport-error for a call that failed in transport after the refill rounds, which is never counted as a miss (no such call occurred in run 6)
method.harnessRun6: scripts/measure-skill-trigger.mjs --mode direct: one chat-completions call per run to the local OpenAI-compatible gateway, with the same routing prompt and catalog as before and no agent runtime around it. A call through omp carried about 180K input tokens of the runtime's own prompt; a direct call carries about 4.1K to 4.7K. An answer that is neither a catalog name nor none is re-asked up to 2 times; calls that fail in transport are refilled in up to 2 rounds and leave the row open (exit 3) instead of counting as a miss.
method.modelRun6: group/deepseek-v4.1-flash (gateway group of the same model family)
method.thresholdRun6: trigger >= 8/10 hits; no_trigger <= 2/10 hits. The 30-run probes use trigger >= 24/30 and no_trigger <= 6/30.
method.caseSourceRun6: design set: skills/hyper-handoff/assets/evals/hyper-handoff-cases.jsonl, 48 cases (the 36 of run 5 plus 12 added in commit 400c9a4d before the wording work); holdout set: skills/hyper-handoff/assets/evals/hyper-handoff-holdout-cases.jsonl, 24 cases pinned in commit de94f823 before the wording work, written by a separate agent, not read while the wording was designed, and measured once after the wording was frozen in commit c479eead
method.rawRunsRun6: scripts/fixtures/skill-trigger-runs/hyper-handoff/ holds the raw output of every run 6 measurement and, under descriptions/, the description variants that were measured. The raw files record the catalog name each call answered, so they are kept outside the skill directory, which must not name other skills.
method.catalogRun6: 28 skills, the catalog of the branch base f407dd86, for 07 and 08; both sets were measured again on the 31-skill catalog of dev 7bf50b8f (09 and 10) after the branch was rebased onto it.

triggerRuns.changeBeforeRun: The prompt of the case hyper-handoff-boundary-loop-state-ko was rewritten to carry a handoff signal; the rest of the fixture was unchanged.

newRows.note: Rows added to the fixture after run 2; this is their first measurement.

triggerRuns.changeBeforeRun: The skill text moved from daf0b2d5 to f866f9d8 and the fixture grew from 19 to 36 cases; every case was run again on the new text.

followUpProbe.note: This row passed run 3 at 3/3 and failed run 4 at 1/3. It names a memo, so the new exclusion does not apply to it; six more calls of the same routing prompt on the same text answered hyper-handoff every time, so the run 4 miss is read as sampling variation, and the wording was not changed for it. The probe is not part of the run 4 count.

triggerRuns.changeBeforeRun: The description and the routing rule in SKILL.md and SKILL.ko.md were reworded: reading, restating, or continuing from a memo under .hyper/handoff/ is named as a trigger, the three-line restatement is named, and a plain request to continue that names no memo while none is open is excluded. The fixture was unchanged; every case was run again on the new text.

triggerRuns.rule: trigger rows pass at 4/5 or more hits, no_trigger rows at 1/5 or fewer

earlierRounds.note: description was 1124 chars, over the 1024 limit of the standards gate, so the text was shortened and this result was discarded

triggerRuns.changeBeforeRun: The description in SKILL.md and SKILL.ko.md gained a clause: a named memo routes here even when its HEAD or dirty files no longer match the repository, and the mismatch is reported. The clause sits in the resume trigger and the description is 1016 characters.

triggerRuns.rule: trigger rows pass at 8/10 or more hits, no_trigger rows at 2/10 or fewer

catalog31.note: Same description text and harness settings as the 28-skill runs; the three skills added to dev drew no answer in either set. Every row scored 10/10 or 0/10. Observed answers per call are in the raw files.

triggerRuns.probeNote: Probes were made before the wording was frozen and chose it. 01 and 03 are the run 5 text (1016 characters) on the 36 and the 12 new design cases; 02 and 04 are that text cut to its first sentence (419 characters), to the 86-character summary one runtime shows, and to 250 bytes; 05 is two candidate texts in full and cut to 250 bytes on the 48 design cases; 06 repeats the 12 no_trigger design rows at 30 runs for four texts and has no trigger rows. A failed entry reads '<id> <hits>/<runs>'.
triggerRuns.changeBeforeRun: The description in SKILL.md and SKILL.ko.md was reordered: the first sentence now holds the trigger (work passes to a fresh session, agent, or machine through a state memo) together with the exclusion of a plain request to continue that names no memo while none is open; the signals, including the stale-fingerprint clause, follow in the second sentence. The description is 1006 characters and its first sentence 243. Cut probes showed that trigger rows barely depend on the description length (1,075 of 1,080 trigger calls over six cut runs), while the exclusion at the end of the run 5 text weakened when the text was cut.

coldReads.detail: The reader could not name how to re-run the cases from the memo (question 4) and gave a rules path that did not resolve (question 6).
The reader named the next action with its file list, the done-when conditions, and the repository, branch, worktree, and state pointers.

limits: Selection was measured among skill names only, with the catalog supplied directly; the router path was not exercised.
expected.must behavior was not measured; only the chosen skill name was recorded.
Runs 3 and 4 are each one pass of 3 calls per case, so a case's rate has four possible values and no interval target was set.
Run 4 follows a wording change written against the two rows that failed run 3, so those two rows are not held-out evidence for the new wording; the other 34 rows are.
Runs 1 and 2 describe the earlier text at daf0b2d5 and run 3 the text at f866f9d8; they were not re-run and their numbers were copied from the earlier record.
Both cold reads were made on a memo written under the earlier text and were not repeated for f866f9d8 or 5ac4a9db.
Run 5 follows wording changes written against rows that failed earlier rounds, so those rows are not held-out evidence for the new wording.
Run 5 is one pass of 5 calls per case; rows at exactly 4/5 could land below the bar on a repeat.
Runs 1-4 used harness copies under /tmp/handoff-eval-run that may no longer exist; run 5 reproduces with scripts/measure-skill-trigger.mjs.
Run 6 calls the model directly with the routing prompt. Selection inside a real agent session, where the runtime may shorten or drop descriptions, was not measured.

Run 6 was first measured on the 28-skill catalog of the branch base f407dd86. After the branch was rebased onto dev 7bf50b8f, which adds three skills (31 in total), both sets were measured again once at 10 calls per case and passed unchanged (holdout 24/24, design 48/48). Adding skills changes the catalog again.
The 12 design cases of run 6 and the candidate probes chose the wording, so only the 24 holdout cases are an independent check; they were measured once, 10 calls per case.

The 30-run probes of run 6 cover only the 12 no_trigger design rows; every trigger row is a 10-run value. The same 250-byte text scored 3/10 and 2/10 on one no_trigger row in two 10-run passes, so a row near the bar needs more runs before it is judged.

That the 4/5 rows of run 5 came from the agent-mode harness and not from the wording is an inference: the same text scored 10/10 on both rows in direct mode, but the run 5 method was not repeated at 10 runs.
